0|b3eb04be729982ae7e311afcc9c031eca4718a46|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"mlxsw: spectrum_port_range: Add port range core
The Spectrum ASICs have a fixed number of port range registers
which maintains the following parameters:
* Minimum and maximum port.
* Apply port range for source port
* Apply port range for TCP
* Apply port range for IPv4
Implement a port range core which takes care of the allocation and
configuration of these registers and exposes an API that allows
in-driver consumers (e.g.
column2: the ACL code) to request matching on a range

column1: of either source or destination port.
These registers are going to be used for port range matching in the
flower classifier that already matches on EtherType being IPv4 / IPv6 and
IP protocol being TCP / UDP. As such
column2: there is no need to limit these

column1: registers to a specific EtherType or IP protocol
the likelihood of a register being shared by multiple flower filters.
It is unlikely that a filter will match on the same range of both source
and destination ports
column2: which is why each register is only configured to

column1: match on either source or destination port. If a filter requires
matching on a range of both source and destination ports
utilize two port range registers and match on the output of both.
For efficient lookup and traversal
column2: use XArray to store the allocated

column1: port range registers. The XArray uses RCU and an internal spinlock to
synchronise access
column2: so there is no need for a dedicate lock.
